pools.form.templateDesc: The sandbox template that defines the runtime environment, base image, and resource configuration for pods in this pool.
pools.form.imageOverrideDesc: Overrides the image defined in the template for all pods in this pool. Useful for testing a new image version without modifying the shared template.
pools.form.resourceMultiplierDesc: Scales CPU and memory requests by this integer factor. For example, a multiplier of 2 doubles the template's resource allocation per sandbox.
pools.form.quotaDesc: Associates this pool with a quota group for resource accounting. Required by the selected template.
pools.form.imagePullSecretDesc: Optional. Configure registry credentials to avoid 429 rate limits when pulling from DockerHub, GHCR, or other private registries. The credentials are stored in a Secret with the same lifecycle as this pool.

pools.form.nameDescShort: Unique name for this pool. Must follow Kubernetes naming rules (lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens).
pools.form.autoscalingDesc: Automatically adjust the number of idle pods based on demand.
pools.form.autoscalingEnabledDesc: When enabled, the pool size adjusts automatically within min/max replica bounds.
pools.form.minReplicasDesc: Minimum number of idle pods to keep running. Must be ≥ 0.
pools.form.maxReplicasDesc: Maximum number of idle pods. Must be ≥ min replicas.
pools.form.scaleUpModeDesc: Conservative: +1/decision; Default: +⌈n/2⌉/decision; Aggressive: double up to maxReplicas.

pools.form.idleThresholdSecondsDesc: Proactively scale up when idle count stays at 0 for this many seconds. Set 0 to disable.
pools.form.idleTimeoutSecondsDesc: Seconds a pod must remain idle before it becomes a scale-down candidate.

prometheus.desiredTooltip: Total number of pre-warmed sandbox slots currently allocated across all pools. Includes Idle, Starting, and Stopping sandboxes.
prometheus.runningTooltip: Sandboxes actively being used by an AI agent right now.
prometheus.idleTooltip: Warm sandboxes sitting in the pool, ready to be claimed instantly with near-zero startup latency.
prometheus.startingTooltip: Sandboxes being initialized. Not yet available for claims.
prometheus.stoppingTooltip: Sandboxes that have been released and are being recycled back to Idle state.
prometheus.failedTooltip: Sandboxes that encountered an unrecoverable error and are pending replacement.
prometheus.startRateTooltip: Rate of successfully created sandboxes over a rolling 5-minute window (ops/s).
prometheus.peak1hTooltip: Maximum number of concurrently running sandboxes observed in the last 1 hour.
prometheus.peak24hTooltip: Maximum number of concurrently running sandboxes observed in the last 24 hours.
prometheus.replicaTrendTooltip: How the pool's replica counts evolve over time across all phases: Desired (desired), Running (claimed), Starting (warming up), Stopping (recycling), and Idle (ready).
prometheus.claimDurationTooltip: Time from a sandbox claim request to the sandbox reaching Running state. Lower is better. P99 spikes may indicate slow initialization or resource contention.
prometheus.startingDurationTooltip: Time from claim to Running (image pull + container start). Only successful startups are charted; canceled sandboxes never reached Running.
prometheus.runningDurationTooltip: How long sandboxes stay in Running state before being released. Reflects AI agent workload duration.
prometheus.recycleDurationTooltip: Time for a released sandbox to complete cleanup and return to the Idle pool. High P99 suggests slow teardown or heavy recycle hooks.
prometheus.createRateTooltip: Per-second rate of sandbox create requests broken down by outcome: Success (sandbox claimed from pool), No Idle (pool exhausted), Error (internal failure).
prometheus.deleteRateTooltip: Per-second rate of sandbox deletions broken down by stop reason: Completed (task finished), Canceled (explicitly stopped), Released (idle timeout / auto-expiry), Failed (OOM, crash, eviction).
prometheus.scheduleSuccessRateTooltip: Per-second rate of sandbox scheduling attempts (Idle→Running) by outcome: Success, Conflict (version or phase mismatch, usually retried), Error (internal failure).
prometheus.recycleSuccessRateTooltip: Per-second rate of sandbox recycling attempts (Stopping→Idle) by outcome: Success, Conflict (version or phase mismatch, usually retried), Error (internal failure).
prometheus.scheduleDispatchLatencyToolti: Time from create request enqueue to the scheduler CAS goroutine start (P99/P95/P90/P50). Measures how quickly the pool scheduler picks up and dispatches a request. High P99 indicates the scheduler is under pressure or the ready queue is exhausted.
prometheus.scheduleQueueSizeTooltip: Current number of idle pods in the ready queue (available for immediate dispatch) and inflight reservations (pods being CAS'd or recently claimed). Rising reservations with a stable queue indicates high concurrent dispatch.
prometheus.scheduleCasOutcomeTooltip: Per-second rate of TriggerUpdateWithOptions outcomes from the streaming scheduler: Success (pod claimed), Retriable (phase mismatch or k8s conflict — retried automatically), Hard (unrecoverable error). A rising Hard rate warrants investigation.
prometheus.scheduleRefreshRateTooltip: Per-second rate of per-pool ready-queue refresh attempts: OK (refreshed normally), Throttled (skipped due to cooldown window), Error (refresh failed). High Throttled rate is normal under load; sustained Errors indicate scrape or API issues.
prometheus.scheduleInternalCountersToolt: Per-second rate of scheduler housekeeping events. TTL Expired: reservations removed by TTL sweep — the CAS success path intentionally keeps the reservation so the informer cache can catch up, so TTL Expired ≈ dispatch rate is normal. Scale-Down Skip: pods skipped during refresh due to the scale-down-protected annotation. Queue Evicted: pods discarded at dispatch time because they were absent from the informer cache or no longer Idle (e.g. deleted during scale-down).
prometheus.createTotalTooltip: Total sandbox create attempts in the selected window, including successful, throttled (no idle pod), and errored results.
prometheus.envoyUpstreamTooltip: Total upstream requests forwarded through Envoy Gateway in the selected window.
prometheus.peakEnvoyQpsTooltip: Peak Envoy upstream request rate (req/s) observed in the selected window, based on a 5-minute rolling average.
prometheus.envoyTxBytesTooltip: Total bytes sent to upstream connections by Envoy in the selected window (envoy_cluster_upstream_cx_tx_bytes_total).
prometheus.envoyRxBytesTooltip: Total bytes received from upstream connections by Envoy in the selected window (envoy_cluster_upstream_cx_rx_bytes_total).
prometheus.envoyBandwidthRateTooltip: Real-time bandwidth throughput of Envoy upstream connections (bytes/s). TX is the send rate, RX is the receive rate. Sustained high values may indicate upstream traffic pressure.
prometheus.envoyUpstreamRateTooltip: Rate of upstream requests forwarded through Envoy Gateway (ops/s), split by HTTP response code class: 2xx success, 4xx client errors, 5xx server errors.
prometheus.envoyErrorRateTooltip: Fraction of Envoy upstream requests returning 4xx or 5xx responses over time. A sustained high 5xx rate may indicate upstream service issues.
prometheus.envoyLatencyTooltip: End-to-end latency percentiles (milliseconds) for Envoy upstream requests. Rising P99 may indicate slow upstream responses or network jitter.
prometheus.sandboxCreateErrorRateTooltip: Proportion of sandbox create attempts by outcome over time: Success (created normally), No Idle (throttled — no pre-warmed pod), and Error (internal failure). Rising No Idle % indicates pool capacity shortage; rising Error % indicates controller issues.
prometheus.sandboxDeleteFailRateTooltip: Proportion of sandbox deletions by stop reason over time: Completed (normal), Failed (OOM/crash/eviction), Released (idle timeout), and Canceled (explicit stop). A sustained high Failed % warrants investigation of node resource pressure or image issues.

envs.form.updateStrategy.hint: Automatically roll idle pods onto the new revision when the template or image / network overrides change.
envs.form.updateStrategy.autoUpdateDescr: When off, idle pods stay on their current revision until you re-enable it.
envs.form.updateStrategy.maxUnavailableD: Absolute count (3) or percentage (20%) of idle pods that may be rebuilt at once.
envs.form.imagePullSecret.hint: Write-only credentials. Server materialises a dockerconfigjson Secret named ips-{envName} (OwnerRef = Env, cascade-deleted on Env delete) and stamps it into every member Pool. Leave rows empty to keep existing Secret unchanged.
envs.form.imagePullSecret.empty: No credentials. Add a row to provide image-pull authentication for private registries.
envs.form.networkPolicy.hint: Control the sandbox's outbound (egress) network. Enforced by an in-Pod filter sidecar.
envs.form.networkPolicy.modeDescription: Unrestricted allows all outbound; Disable blocks all; Allowlist permits only the domains/IPs you list.
envs.form.networkPolicy.unrestrictedPriv: Unrestricted reaches private ranges too (RFC1918, cluster-internal addresses), same as a sandbox with no network policy — so enabling credential injection never narrows what the sandbox can reach. To allow every host while keeping the anti-SSRF baseline, choose Allowlist with the domain "*" instead.
envs.form.networkPolicy.allowedDomainsDe: One per line. Exact (pypi.org) or wildcard (*.pythonhosted.org). DNS is permitted automatically.
envs.form.networkPolicy.allowPrivateNetw: Disables the default block of RFC1918 / metadata ranges. Leave off for anti-SSRF protection.
envs.form.secretInjection.hint: The filter sidecar adds these headers to matching outbound requests. The sandbox can use the credential but can never read it — values stay in Secrets and are delivered outside the sandbox.
envs.form.secretInjection.hasErrors: Fix the highlighted credential injection fields.
envs.form.secretInjection.usableNotReada: Note: the sandbox cannot read the credential, but it can use its privileges without limit. Narrow with path prefixes where possible.
envs.form.secretInjection.credNameDescri: How rules refer to it: {{ name }}. Letters, digits, - and _ only — it is also the key inside this Env's credential Secret.
envs.form.secretInjection.valueKeep: leave blank to keep the stored value
envs.form.secretInjection.valueDescripti: Stored in this Env's credential Secret (one Secret per Env, one key per credential) and never shown again.
envs.form.secretInjection.exposeAsDescri: Optional. Environment variable the sandbox receives, holding a decoy instead of this value. Needed only when the client checks the variable is set.
envs.form.secretInjection.placeholderDes: Optional. The decoy value. Set one when the client validates the credential's shape before sending; at least 16 characters.
envs.form.errors.injectionCredentialName: Letters, digits, - and _ only, starting with a letter or digit
envs.form.errors.injectionValueRequired: A value is required for a new credential
envs.form.errors.injectionCredentialInco: Name, Secret and Key are all required
envs.form.errors.placeholderTooShort: Placeholder must be at least 16 characters
envs.form.errors.placeholderNeedsExposeA: A placeholder needs an env var to expose it
envs.form.errors.injectionWildcardHost: Wildcards are not allowed for injection hosts
envs.form.errors.injectionHostNotAllowed: Host is not in the egress allowlist, so the traffic is blocked before injection runs
envs.form.errors.injectionValueNeedsCred: Use a {{ credential }} reference — a literal value would be a plaintext secret
envs.form.errors.injectionUnknownCredent: References a credential that is not declared above
envs.form.name: Name
envs.form.nameDescription: RFC 1123 DNS label. Members are Pools created under this name.
envs.form.templateDescription: Cluster-scoped SandboxTemplate this Env binds to. Its Pod spec, runtimes, and docs are the base; per-field overrides below apply uniformly to every member Pool.
envs.form.templateNoDescription: No description provided for this template.
envs.form.imageDescription: Overrides the main container image of the rendered Template. Leave empty to keep the template's image. Takes effect for Pods created or upgraded after this change.
envs.form.podCreationImagePolicyDescript: IdleImage (default) uses spec.idleImage so new Pods start pre-warmed with this Env's image. PoolDefaultImage uses the template container image for first boot, then upgrades in place to the env image.
envs.form.defaultStartupTimeoutDescripti: Max time a Sandbox may spend in the Starting phase before it is marked Failed. Format: 30s, 5m, 1h. Members may override per-Pool.
envs.form.defaultIdleTimeoutDescription: Max time a Sandbox may stay Running with no activity before it is auto-stopped and returned to the warm pool. Format: 30s, 5m, 1h.
envs.form.overridesHint: Shared across every member Pool (image, image policy, default timeouts).
envs.form.membersHint: Each row materialises one SandboxPool. Use different quotas / inline resources to mix sizing within the same Env.
envs.form.noMembersHint: No members declared. The Reconciler will create a single namesake Pool using the Env Overrides.
envs.form.member.name: Pool name
envs.form.errors.nameTooLong: Name must be 24 characters or fewer (pool names derive from it).

envs.editAutoscaling.title: Edit Autoscaling — {{name}}
envs.editAutoscaling.description: Update the group-level autoscaling policy. The Env autoscaler picks up the change on its next reconcile cycle (≤ 10s).
envs.editAutoscaling.field.enabledDesc: When off, member Pool replicas are managed manually via spec.replicas.
envs.editAutoscaling.field.scaleUpModeDe: Conservative: +1 per decision. Default: +max(1, ceil(N/2)). Aggressive: double up to maxReplicas.
envs.editAutoscaling.field.minReplicasDe: Lower bound on the sum of spec.replicas across every member in this group. Setting to 0 lets the autoscaler shrink the group to zero pods when there's no demand.
envs.editAutoscaling.field.maxReplicasDe: Upper bound on the sum of spec.replicas across every member in this group. Leave empty for no ceiling. Required when Scale-up Mode is Aggressive — doubling without a ceiling is unsafe.
envs.editAutoscaling.field.idleZeroQuiet: Suppresses proactive scale-up when no Sandbox.Create request has been observed for a Pool within this many seconds — keeps an unused warm pool from staying spun up. Reactive scale-ups (a request is already queued with no idle pod) ignore this window. Set to 0 to disable.
envs.editAutoscaling.field.cooldownSecon: Minimum time between two consecutive successful scale-ups on the same Pool. Prevents the autoscaler from over-shooting when capacity arrives in bursts.
envs.editAutoscaling.field.idleThreshold: How long idleReplicas must remain at 0 before the proactive scale-up trigger fires. Set to 0 to disable proactive scale-up; only reactive demand (queued claim requests) will then grow the Pool.
envs.editAutoscaling.field.saturationCoo: After the cluster admission probe reports it can't fit more replicas, the autoscaler skips re-probing for this long. Stops the controller from hammering the plugin chain when capacity is genuinely exhausted.
envs.editAutoscaling.field.idleTimeoutSe: An idle Pod becomes a scale-down candidate only after it has been idle for at least this long. Set short for aggressive shrinkage; set long to give bursty workloads time to reclaim warm pods.
envs.editAutoscaling.field.stabilization: Minimum time between two consecutive scale-downs on the same Pool. Prevents thrashing when load fluctuates around the trigger boundary.
envs.editAutoscaling.field.protectionWin: After an idle Pod is selected for scale-down, it carries a protection annotation for this long before deletion. A new Sandbox.Create arriving in this window can still claim it, cancelling the scale-down.

managedAgents.form.namespaceDesc: Leave empty to use the agent's namespace.

vault.title: Vault
vault.description: Credentials a sandbox can use but never read. Reference one from a network rule and the egress proxy substitutes the real value into the outbound request; the sandbox only ever sees the placeholder.
vault.apiKeyRequired: The vault is served by the E2B-compatible API, which authenticates with API keys only. Create one to manage secrets here.
vault.valueWriteOnly: Write-only. No API returns a stored value, so it cannot be shown again — rotate it if you lose it.

vault.empty.title: No secrets yet
vault.empty.description: Add one, then reference it from a sandbox's network rules to inject it into outbound requests.

vault.create.description: The name becomes the reference used in network rules. The value is stored write-only.
vault.rotate.title: Rotate secret
vault.rotate.description: Replaces the stored value and increments the version. Running sandboxes keep the value they were armed with; the new one applies from the next sandbox.
vault.delete.title: Delete secret
vault.delete.description: Sandbox creations that reference this secret will fail. Running sandboxes are unaffected; their credentials are erased when they are released.
